notes:
v2.9.0 keeps money customers pay in advance out of Accounts Receivable, fixes the cash-basis BAS for prepayments, and keeps you signed in after an update.

Customer prepayments in Income in Advance: money a customer pays before you invoice them, and anything they pay over what an invoice owes, is owed back to them until it's used. It now sits in a new liability account, 2-1600 Income in Advance, instead of reducing Accounts Receivable. It moves to the invoice when you apply it (More > Apply Credit), dated on the invoice date. This works from Record Payment on an invoice (paying more than owing now tells you how much will be held), Payments > New Receipt with no invoice, and Bank Rec (Hold $X as a prepayment, or Money in to Income in Advance with the customer as Who). Credit already held in your file is moved into the new account the first time you open it.

Cash-basis BAS fix: a prepayment applied to an invoice in a later quarter was counted on the date the money came in, so its GST and sales could land in a quarter you'd already reported. It's now counted when the prepayment is applied to the invoice. The cash-basis Profit & Loss and the GST drill-down are fixed too. If you report GST on a cash basis and have applied a prepayment to an invoice in a later quarter, check that quarter's BAS.

Overpaying an invoice: paying more than an invoice owed pushed its paid amount over the total. The invoice is now paid in full and the rest is held as a prepayment.

Staying signed in after an update: the restart after an update now comes back signed in when you opened your file from the startup page, not only when Dogbox was started with the file. This update itself is installed by the old version, so it will still ask you to sign in once; later updates won't.

The Invoices and Bank Reconciliation guides under Help cover prepayments and overpayments.
